Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful to see the routing & fallback behavior. A couple of things came out of our internal readout that I want to put on the table as we scope a short POC:

- Our product needs two distinct SLO buckets:
  * Fast queries (UI search / short summarization): target p95 <= 250ms, typical output <= 256 tokens.
  * Long-form generation (report exports): target p95 <= 1.5s, outputs can be up to 4k tokens occasionally.
- We care about tail (p99) for business-critical flows; p99 should not exceed 3s for long-form if possible.
- We will feed the model documents (tokenized inputs with metadata) — the effective context length is often input+output and can spike above 12k tokens for certain use cases.
- Two questions for planning:
  1) How much extra tail latency should we expect when output length increases from 512 -> 4k tokens in a non-streaming response?
  2) When using streaming, what latency guarantees can you provide for the first token and for steady-state throughput while streaming long outputs?

Can you share a simple heatmap or table that illustrates expected p50/p95/p99 as a function of (context size, output length) and whether streaming is enabled? Also, we'd like a clear list of the perf tests you propose (synthetic workload shape, concurrency, run length) so we can approve the POC.

We looped Raj (CTO) in on cc for visibility — he'll be a final approver on the test scope.

Thanks,
Amelia

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 6:42 PM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've CC'd Ben (our performance lead) to give numbers and the test plan. The attached heatmap is an initial estimate — we'll refine after a quick smoke run.

Thanks — quick technical summary and proposed measurement definitions so we are all aligned:

Measurement basics
- Tokens: we count input + output tokens for pricing and for estimating working memory; for latency the important axis is output length and peak working set (input + kv cache).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: non-streaming calculates full output then returns it as one response (tail = sum of token generation time). Streaming returns tokens as they are generated (first-byte latency dominated by model init + first-token decode).

Back-of-envelope latency numbers (on Redwood Dedicated capacity, optimized kernels):
- Short outputs (<=256 tokens), context <= 2k tokens: p50 ~ 60–90ms, p95 ~ 180–260ms, p99 ~ 350–500ms.
- Medium outputs (512–1k tokens), context <= 4k tokens: p50 ~ 120–200ms, p95 ~ 400–700ms, p99 ~ 800–1.5s.
- Long outputs (2k–4k tokens), context up to 12k tokens: non-streaming p95 1.2–2.5s (depending on kernel/quant), p99 can hit 3–6s on heavy tail.

Streaming behavior (typical):
- First token latency for long outputs: 120–300ms (model init + first decode); thereafter tokens stream at steady-state token/sec determined by model throughput and micro-batching.
- With streaming, user-visible time-to-first-byte is usually within your short SLO; time-to-complete will still be proportional to output length but perceived latency is lower because users see partial results early.

Operational notes and levers
- Batching (larger batches) improves throughput but increases head latency; use adaptive continuous batching to meet p95 targets.
- KV caching for repeated context prefixes reduces effective context cost if you have repeated document prefixes.
- Quantization reduces per-token time but may change peak memory profile.
- Concurrency tuning: for your 200 rps target with 50 concurrent users, we recommend initial concurrency cap of 64 and a concurrency-based admission policy.

Proposed perf test (what we'll run)
1) Smoke run (30m): 50 RPS, mixed 80/20 short/long, streaming enabled for long outputs — capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec.
2) Soak run (60m): 200 RPS, concurrency 64, 50% long outputs up to 4k tokens, both streaming and non-streaming variants.
3) Tail-run (30m): burst traffic to evaluate p99 behavior and model fallback.

Deliverables after runs
- Heatmaps (context vs output length) with p50/p95/p99 annotated (png).
- CSV with raw latency samples and request shapes (perf-test-plan.csv).
- Recommendations: batching/streaming settings and canary config for production.

I'll attach the perf-test-plan.csv (request shapes) and we can iterate.

—Ben

- Token counting: we include some extra metadata tokens (JSON blobs) in front of requests — is the heatmap sensitive to a 10–20% metadata bloat on input?

If those are straightforward, we'll greenlight the soak and provide a sample dataset by EOD.
